summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant, chronic heart failure, complete heart block, and prior infections was readmitted one day after discharge due to bleeding and pain at the abdominal incision site following explant of a pacemaker generator. He had recently undergone placement of a Micra leadless pacemaker and removal of the abdominal device. Examination revealed a hematoma at the incision site, likely aggravated by coughing and hiccups. He underwent successful evacuation of the hematoma and cauterization of the bleeding source. His postoperative course was stable, with controlled pain, no further bleeding, and resumption of aspirin. He continued all baseline medications, including immunosuppressants, heart failure, and diabetes therapies. He was discharged home with a pressure dressing, a one-week course of cephalexin, activity restrictions, and follow-up in the device clinic.
